seed_sweep.interpretation: No check changes verdict on either seed set, and two default runs give identical PASS/FAIL lines (IDENTICAL_VERDICTS; only the timing header differs). Real, seed-specific game bugs appear consistently: the terminal check misses cavetest555 x3 (cells 38,0 / 35,0 / 39,20) and cavetest8 (cell 20,0), all the N8 edge-ring cause. Cave gold stays tier-blind at 1.02x / 0.99x; surface gold holds at 1.53x / 1.58x. There is one harness fragility and it did not flip a verdict: on seed 8 a surface equipment chest is classified as a cave chest ('103/103 equipment rewards (102 surface, 1 cave)'; cave 'common ... equip1').

suspicions: pressA casts the current spell on every A press (_tryCastSpell, L19192), and coin drops are vacuumed within 18 u (coins++, L11105). Near Endless enemies a kill or a coin drop could change coins during the press ticks, making the floor check's 'paid === gold' fail, or the cap check's 'looted = coins !== c0' pass, for the wrong reason. Not observed in any run.
The cave-gold and equipment-quality checks read generateChunk objects like the epic check does (p9), so a window-level fix would be missed. Only the epic check was demonstrated.

The reserve check picks LAB.entrances()[0] from every generated network, which may lie outside the window on some seeds. The control chest should turn that into a FAIL rather than a silent PASS. It passed on 12345, 31337 and 2024.
Overlap with game_persistence_harness.js (author's concern): the same two chest-swap defects are known bugs in both suites, so a fix has to clear both lists.

per_check.id: physics: floor picker never fabricates ground at h=0 for a cell that has walkable layers
per_check.why: It calls the game's own getWalkableLayerTopAt on every cell and neighbour-top pair (1,562,400 pairs). The only way to get {topH:0,idx:-1,type:0} is the no-candidate branch at L7901, i.e. every walkable layer is more than STEP_UP above. The existing D11 picker FIX flips it. Caveat: it fixes WHERE the repair must go (the picker). A step()-side fix that blocks the move (my probe p_block) removes the U2 symptom but leaves A1 FAIL. That is defensible, because four callers use the sentinel's topH (L10147 airborne landing, L10176 edge fall, L10272 ground ease, L19356 underground detection). It also only tests from the neighbour's TOP layer, so it undercounts cave-floor-to-cave-floor rises.
per_check.evidence: p_block run: 'FAIL physics: floor picker never fabricates ground ... 29 of 1562400' while the walk-based symptom is gone (METRIC max_grounded_rise_per_tick 0). a_approach.js + p_d11fix: 'PASS ... 0 of 1562400'.

missing_checks: E2 IS reproduced in the SURFACE/cap layer near entrances. The per-chunk entrance blur (L5524-5562, neighbours clipped at the chunk edge) seams the pre-stamp surface, which also sets cap Z and the feather's blend source. Within 300 u of entrances, the max border spike is 0.12-0.21 h vs 0.012-0.016 on control lines, and the mean positive spike is 0.034-0.077 vs 0.0004-0.0006. Beyond 700 u, border equals control (e.g. 0.019 vs 0.026). Evidence: scratch surf_seam.js 'ct424242 surfaceH within 300u of entrances: border n 90 maxSpike 0.178 meanPos 0.0772 ... | control n 300 maxSpike 0.016 meanPos 0.0004'. No check covers caps or surface; the floor-under-ceiling seam check cannot see it.

Full-cell truncation differential: every cell of every generated chunk should have a ceiling iff queryCaveGeometry(corner, all nets, 2.0).ceilZ !== null. Today there are 0 mismatches over 941 chunks. It catches trunc_row and trunc_chamber_margin; the current probe-point check misses the latter.
E4 (cap lifted above natural terrain by the L6693 clamp) is only a METRIC: 4,555 caps, max +2.24 h (ct777 (174,798)). Nothing decides the audit's suspected side-entry / false-underground effect.

Entrance approach overlaps its own network's cave interior. ct777 e#1: along 300 is a corridor core with fade 1.000 and floor -7.19; along 470 is a chamber feather with fade 0.460. Whole approaches are roofed on ct777 e#1, ct5 e#0 and ct31337 e#1 (CT seed sweep). This is a U1 entrance-placement defect with no check of its own; today it contaminates the roof, path-step and walk-out verdicts.

Layer actually walked on the way in: the picker chain on ct777 e#1 stands on the cap until along 32, then drops 7.90 h in one cell at along 26, which counts as 'walk' under STEP_DOWN=10. Nothing checks the max single-cell change of the chain, or that it never stands on a roof cap in the approach (walk_profile.js).
N14 (STEP_DOWN relaxed only within 260 u vs the 480 u approach) is not exercised by the default seeds. Normal seed 123 exposes it at along 284 (1.53 h drop).

F6 (ceilinged but uncarved grid walls): there is no check that ceilinged cells and grid[] carving agree. From the default detail, 52,757 ceilinged - 9,123 with no floor under the ceiling = 43,634, of which only 43,470 are open. That leaves at least 164 grid-wall cells carrying a floor+ceiling stack (derived arithmetic, not a separate measurement).

D11 fallback: the walk-out chain shows 'fall to 0.00' (idx -1 with no candidate returns topH 0, L7901) on every break, but no verdict asserts that the no-candidate case never yields a target above the player.
harness_bugs: game_lab CLI cannot pass --networks or --normal-seeds. 'python3 -m tools.webui.game_lab caves_geometry --networks 3' fails with 'error: unrecognized arguments: --networks 3', yet the test docstring (test_game_caves_geometry.py L15-16) and the harness usage (L17) advertise them. --seeds only changes the Cave Test seeds (harness L39), so a CLI seed sweep never varies the normal-Endless worlds; I had to call run_harness(args=[...]) directly.

Harness L464-468 assumes the nearest network has at least one entrance ('var near = found[k], E = null ... LAB.placeWorld(E.x, E.y, "top")'). With zero entrances (probe vac_no_entrances) both normal scenarios crash: 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'x')'. It should record a PRECONDITION instead.

Walk-out endpoint rule (L343 surf = LAB.topWalkable(sls[0]); L356 Math.abs(co.h - surf.z) < 1e-3) fails entrances with zero unsupported steps when the +470 cell has a cap over a cave floor. Today on seed 5: 'ct5 e0,0#0 out: unsupported=0 ends h -0.22 (surface 0.29)'. In probe worlds: 'ct424242 out: unsupported=0 ends h -0.96 (surface 1.50)'.

The path-step profile uses lowestWalkableZ (L316), which on roofed approaches is the cave floor under the cap rather than the layer the player walks (ct777 e#1: the picker stands on the cap to along 32).

The truncation probe points (L396-417) sample only corridor centre lines and hard edges and chamber centres and rims. That makes the verdict blind to feather-band truncation (probe trunc_chamber_margin: suite PASS, full-cell differential finds 1,311 missing ceilings in n999983).

KNOWN_BUGS text misattributes causes. Path-step says the remaining 3 include 'two entrance trees with different depths', but with tree depths unified (fix_d1_depths) exactly 3 remain and all are feather slope (1.35 / 1.26 / 1.12 h). Walk-out attributes all 8 to D1, but ct777 e#1 fails inside its own network's chamber feather (along 446) once the D1 step-ups are relaxed.
Cosmetic: local cellWorld and cellCorner (L49-56) duplicate LAB.cellWorld and LAB.cellCorner, which now exist in _game_env.js L642-649.
suspicions: The chamber AABB reach in generateChunk (radius + margin 100, L5353-5364) is 8 u short of the chamber feather (radius + 108). The full-cell differential shows 0 missing ceilings today because the chamber's own corridor AABB (width + 100) covers it, so this is latent only. Not verified for every geometry.

The mouth check is internally consistent but low-value to the user: MOUTH_RADIUS only feeds the debug counter at L5613. Whether a 30 u or a 60 u open hole is the intended design is a product decision; either fix passes.

getWalkableLayerTopAt's 10 h STEP_DOWN relaxation (L7853) means a surface player on the cap is 'walked' through the cap hole with up to 10 h drops. That may be the U6 'janky transition' on roofed approaches. I measured it only on the picker chain, not with step()/physics.

harness_bugs: game_render_harness.js L383 `LAB.tick(3); // enemies update once` is false. Three ticks is 50 ms of virtual time, and enemy AI is throttled at `if (now - e.lastUpdate < 80)` (WebPage_Games.h L11405, with lastUpdate seeded on the first tick), so no enemy decision or floor tracking ever runs before the visibility test. Evidence: probe_run.py p_track.py -> HIGH detail shows 'e.z=0.00' on every hidden enemy after the tracking fix. At 6 ticks, e.z=44.66, 42.41 and 59.11 on e2, e8 and e25.

game_render_harness.js L398-401 teleports only the camera, so the player (and the interest-management centre, L11347-11358, radius viewDist*1.5=1350) stays at spawn. Every high-ground enemy still hidden after a correct tracking fix is 1400-1505 u from the player (enemy_real.js --ticks 6: e3 1476, e24 1400, e5 1437, e15 1505). That state cannot co-occur with a camera 60 u away in play.
game_render_harness.js L402 replicates drawEnemies3D's call (e.z||0) instead of running drawEnemies3D, so a fix at L14006 is invisible (P5: replicated 5/23 hidden vs real 0/23).

roofStart (L137-143) scans inward from +600 and returns the FIRST roof cell, not the start of the roof run contiguous with the tunnel. In the base game every tested axis has one contiguous run (axis_profile.js on 12345, 424242, 1, 777 e0/e1, 31337 e0/e1). Under the D2 geometry probe, however, 777e1 becomes 'ROOF[531..465] | open[462..-3] | ROOF[-6..-60]' and roofStart returns +531, which also moves the ramp stand (rs+24) and the walk start (rs+30) 555 u out.
The roof check's archHere (L247-249) requires deepCaveEntrances to match the network entrance within 1 u, so an arch moved to the roof fails as 'NOT in deepCaveEntrances (PRECONDITION FAILED)' (P10).

_game_env.js L209 `restore: function () { if (saveDepth > 0) saveDepth--; ...}` clamps, so saveDepth-based balance checks cannot see over-restores. P6 walk: saveCalls=28994 restoreCalls=29383 saveDepthDelta=0 and the check PASSes. ctxCounters already has the data.

PROBES entry 2 ('FIX D4 / BREAK bleed-through', remove L12692) is the only probe listed for _RAMP and _ARCHV, but it is not a valid fix: it flips _ABOVE to FAIL. So neither check has a probe showing it passes under a correct fix. P2 and P23 do.

The KNOWN_BUGS text for the ramp check attributes the failure to 12691-12692 (D4) with the roof start as context. A D4-only height-aware renderer fix (P2) still gives 'buriedCaveFloorQuads=0' from the ramp, so the entry should say D2 geometry is required as well.

flipped_checks: render: a camera on the cap above the cave draws no buried cave walls
seed_sweep.interpretation: The only aggregate flip is the walls guard going PASS -> FAIL on seed 1: 'BAD s1 spot world=(1074,438) ... fillsFromCap(h=1.08,ug=0)=8'. That is a real seed-specific game defect (capped walls drawn from the cap), not harness fragility; the spot search is deterministic and engines agree. Its attributed cause (N13, unit mismatch) is contradicted by the P8 probe. Per-entrance lines hidden inside still-FAIL aggregates are worth noting. (a) The ceiling check reports 'ok' on s777e0/e1 and s31337e0/e1 with only 12-20 quads, all open-pit cells (pits hidden -> 0). That is threshold vacuity, not a seed bug: --seeds 777,31337 alone flips the check to PASS while D5 is present. (b) The arch-visible check is ok on s1 and 777 and BAD on 31337e0/e1 (sightLine hides). That is real geometry variation from D2. The default run repeated twice gives identical PASS/FAIL lines, and deno and jsc give identical PASS/FAIL lines and details.

suspicions: N13's cause as recorded in the audit index ('unit mismatch L12052') looks wrong. Converting cam.z to render units (P8, --seeds 1) makes seed 1 worse: fillsFromCap goes from 8 to 19. The camera (h=1.08, physics 103.4, render 87.1) is below these walls' cap (4.30-4.66 h, render 107-116) in either unit. The bleed-through comes from the cull's design (it only skips when the camera is above the cap) combined with wall bases taken from l0, which is the ceiling in the re-sorted stacks (D6). It is not a unit mismatch.

drawCaveEntrance3D draws every deepCaveEntrance within 900 u in front of the camera (L16531-16539), so the arch-visible check could be credited by another entrance's arch on a seed where two arches fall within 900 u of the ramp. Not observed on 777/31337 (arch_attr.js perEntrance=[0,61], [61,0]). Recording with deepCaveEntrances restricted to the entrance under test would remove the risk.

On today's geometry, even an occlusion-correct renderer probably cannot reach the ramp check's >50 buried quads from rs+24, because the ceiling lip at the roof start sits below the ramp eye (s12345: ceiling -1.86 h vs eye h -0.54). It only passed here under the D2 geometry probe (P23). If D2 is fixed some other way, the >50 bar may need re-calibrating.
The archway check stands at the network entrance point (the CAP_EXCL cap hole), not at the arch as drawn. Under a moved-arch D2 fix it would keep measuring the hole, not the arch.

The walk balance check's saveDepth-based measure misses over-restores. At the tested call site (drawTorchGlow3D, save depth 0 on entry) a real canvas ignores the extra restore too, so no real miss has been demonstrated. A nested over-restore inside a pass would be missed, though.

per_check.id: enemies: no enemy spawns embedded in a wall (isInGridWall at its own radius)
per_check.why: The judged radius is the harness's own copy of the movement factor: harness L54 'function wallRad(e) { return 8 * (e.enemyType.size || 1) * 0.6; }'. The game keeps that factor at L11303/L11363/L11443. If a fix changes the game's movement radius, the check keeps measuring the old one. Checks that it fails for the right reason, and that it is not overfit, both came back clean: (a) both embedded Brutes touch plain walls, not gridCave walls, so the cause is F3 and not the F6 ring; (b) a spawn-side fix also flips it, so it does not demand the size change. Detection power on the default seeds is low: only 2 enemies are embedded, both in one world.
per_check.evidence: Probe probe_radius05.py (the game uses eRad*0.5 at all 3 movement sites, so a Brute's wall radius is 5.6 u, under the 6 u half-cell). The game itself now frees the Brute: chase goes 339/340 -> '340/340 reached attack state' and patrol frozen goes 73 -> 71. The check still prints 'FAIL ... 2/340 embedded {"surface.tank":2}'. scratch_a.js: 'EMBED cavewin 424242 tank ug=false @594,3402 touches 248,124(plain)' and '@-126,4434 touches 188,210(plain) 190,210(plain)'. Spawn-site probe probe_spawn9.py: 'PASS ... 0/340 embedded'. Seed sweep 31337,2024,98765: '3/688 embedded'.
per_check.recommended_change: Derive the radius from the game instead of hard-coding 0.6. For example, match LAB.sourceText against /var eWallRad = eRad \* ([\d.]+);/ and /var eRad = 8 \* \(e\.enemyType\.size \|\| 1\);/ and fail loudly when either is missing (or add the LAB.enemyWallRadius the author asked for). missing_checks: F7, reverse direction: a SURFACE enemy aggroes on a player standing on the cave floor below it, through 2D LOS. scratch_c.js prints 'REVERSE-ROOF surface enemy chased a player on the cave floor below: 12/12 (tried 13)'. Nothing in the suite checks this direction.

F7, lateral: a cave enemy aggroes on a player standing on open surface ground 120-200 u away, where the player's cell has no ceiling or cap. scratch_e.js prints 'CAVE-ENEMY-LEAVES-CAVE chased 10/10'. No grid wall lies within 120 u of any cave enemy on 8 rays in three cave worlds (scratch_d2.js 'first-wall kinds {}'), so nothing stops a chasing cave enemy from walking out through rock. The roof check covers only a player directly above the cave.

F2, post-chase return: no check that an enemy returns to patrol after a chase ends with a wall between it and its waypoints (the 'wall alternation' case). The patrol check always starts from spawn positions.

F5: the walk animation is keyed to camera distance, not movement. L14069 reads 'var isMoving = (dist > 10 && dist < eType.chaseRange);' with dist measured from the camera. So frozen enemies still animate, which visually hides U4. No suite references F5/L14069.

N6: nothing asserts that starting Cave Test does not re-centre the window on its first frame. The spawn teleport (L7612-7617) skips updateChunks. A check could wrap LAB.tick(1) in LAB.countCalls('assembleWindow') and expect 0 calls, or count cave enemies still underground after one tick. The suite deliberately avoids this state.
Collision parity in the other direction: nothing stops an over-permissive F6 fix, where enemies ignore walls the surface player is blocked by. The author's crude ring probe is exactly such a fix.
E7: LOS flicker at corners. hasLineOfSight caches for 200 ms on half-cell-quantized, window-local keys (L9937-9946) and is not cleared by assembleWindow. Nothing in the suite exercises it.
harness_bugs: wallRad (harness L54) hard-codes the game's movement factor, 8*size*0.6. probe_radius05 shows the embedded check still reports 2/340 after the game's own movement frees those Brutes (chase 340/340). probe_radius05_sep shows separation still reports 40/240. Derive the factor from LAB.sourceText.

The separation site search (L274-283) takes all 12 sites from the top strip of each window: scratch_sites.js 'grid rows used {"4":9,"10":1,"13":2} of gridH=280'. Every example is at world y=-1386, and cave-window sites never sample the caves.

The chase check's id claims 'reaches attack range', but only a pinned player (no step()) allows it. Under LAB.tick it happens in 4/50 trials (scratch_b.js). The suite's PASS contradicts the physics suite's N2 FAIL.
The roof precondition message 'control never chased' hides D19: under a flag-based fix, 70/76 controls fail because placeWorld re-centred the window and cleared e.underground (probe_losflag.py).
Patrol exclusion label (L552) reads 'excluded(chased/left 350 u)', but L208 also excludes dead enemies and enemies with fewer than 2 waypoints.
TRV.noSubject (L349 and L383) mixes two things: 'no surface enemy in world' and 'subject would be embedded at A after the re-centre'.
In the re-centre scenario, enemies whose chunk falls outside the new window are dropped silently at L501, uncounted (not in notFound or movedExcluded).
suspicions: The LOS cache (_losCache, L9938-9946) is keyed on window-local coordinates, lives 200 ms of virtual time, and is not cleared by assembleWindow or resetEndlessMode. A hasLineOfSight call right after a re-centre or a world rebuild (chase candidate search, roof candidate search) could read a stale answer. I did not observe this changing any verdict.

Roof phase A: if repelFromEnemies pushes the player across a chunk line during the 90 ticks, the tracked enemy object is detached and later aggroAt writes are missed. That could produce a false 'no chase'. Not observed; the onCap check only partly guards against it.
Spawner enemies (L20271-20275) are created with z:0 and no underground flag even when their spawner sits in a cave. None of these checks samples them.

A chase miss in the seed sweep is not an embedded spawn: 'endless 98765 cave surface.tank from 2238,6018 ended 54.3u from player'. The cause is unknown; possibly a wall-corner clip or the gridCave ring. The 95% threshold absorbs it.

per_check.id: persistence: the game keeps no state in browser storage (no localStorage/sessionStorage/IndexedDB/cookies)
per_check.why: It rewards the absence of storage, but the audit lists that absence as a persistence PROBLEM ('## Persistence (H) ... H1 no storage at all', audit_index.md:51-52). Any fix of H1, such as saving settings or a run to localStorage, turns this check FAIL, and test_no_unexpected_failures then reports it as a regression. The regex also scans raw source lines, comments included (harness 231-234), so a comment containing the word 'localStorage' would fail it too.
per_check.evidence: harness 236-239: LAB.check(..., real && hits.length === 0, ...); audit_index.md:52 'H1 no storage at all. H2 enemy deaths lost on eviction...'. The existing BREAK probe #11 only proves the scan finds a reference.
per_check.recommended_change: Stop emitting a PASS/FAIL for this. Report it as NOTE/METRIC ('persistence.storage_refs': hits.length) so the suite still states its scope. If H1 is meant to be fixed, add the desired-behaviour check instead (for example 'settings chosen in the panel survive a page reload') as a KNOWN_BUG.

per_check.id: persistence: the spawn window's guaranteed market/shrine is still there after its chunk is evicted and revisited
per_check.why: It only counts a feature as 'guaranteed' if regenerate() (delete + generateChunk, which APPLIES entityDeltas) lacks it (harness 262-268). It also requires the feature's own chunk to be evicted (evictRoundTrip 198, and 'rt.evicted' at 278). The two natural fixes for N12 therefore both FAIL on a precondition. (a) Record the injected feature as a chunk delta: regenerate() now reproduces it, nothing counts as injected, and the check reports 'PRECONDITION: no seed injected'. (b) Pin the chunk so it is never evicted: 'PRECONDITION: chunk not evicted'. The check can only pass under a fix that re-injects from a registry kept outside chunks/entityDeltas.
per_check.evidence: probe.py fix_guar_delta -> 'FAIL ... PRECONDITION: no seed injected a guaranteed feature; s424242: spawn window already had a market and a shrine (nothing injected)'; probe.py fix_guar_pin -> 'FAIL ... s424242 shrine@chunk -1,1 world(-234.0,726.0): PRECONDITION: chunk not evicted (-1,1)'
per_check.recommended_change: Make the check fix-agnostic (see make_v2.py R3 in scratchpad/review_persistence). Right after the page's first world starts, collect EVERY market and shrine in the spawn window, with world positions. Require at least one market AND one shrine (the guarantee itself). Do a far round trip over ALL 49 spawn-window keys, and accept it as 'far enough' when at least one of them was evicted. Then require every recorded feature back at its world position (within 1 u). Validated in the v2 scratch harness: base FAIL ('shrine@chunk -1,1: GONE after far round trip'), fix_guar_delta PASS, fix_guar_pin PASS, all 17 existing suite probes unchanged except probe 0 (see APPLY). Keep the regenerate()-based 'injected' list only for the RESTART detail.

per_check.id: tools: game script evaluates without throwing
per_check.why: LAB.load returns false on any eval exception and the detail carries LAB.loadError. It is a load gate and needs no probe.

per_check.id: tools: caveCapture reports the floor height of the layer the player is standing on (surface cap and cave floor)
per_check.why: standOn() checks that the player is not airborne and is on a type-4 or type-1 layer within 0.05, with a ceiling above for the floor case. emit() needs at least one cap sample and one floor sample. The check fails only on the cap sample, and the author's FIX probe flips it. Caveat: the on-layer precondition is checked before the LAB.frame() at L181 and not re-checked after it. h and ls are simply re-read at L183-184.
per_check.evidence: baseline: '1/2 wrong (1 on the cap, 1 on the cave floor): ... on cap: standing h 2.73, caveCapture floorH -7.62'. The author's FIX flips it to PASS '0/2 wrong'. The same FIX also flips 'records the player's own height' to PASS (see that check).
per_check.recommended_change: After LAB.frame() at L181, re-run the on-layer test (not airborne, the walkable layer at h is still of `kind`) and skip the sample if it fails. Add "records the player's own height ... : FAIL" to this FIX probe's expect once that check is repaired, so the coupling is guarded.

per_check.id: tools: caveCapture records the world seed
per_check.why: has() looks for the VALUE in every numeric leaf, whatever its key (L289, L293). With --seeds, the first seed can equal a constant that is always in the snapshot: nearestEntranceDist is always 100 (the player stands 100 u inside), and config.gridSize=12, entranceVisRadius=14, ceilBlendStart=60 and so on. The seed-drop BREAK then still passes.
per_check.evidence: seed:null BREAK probe with args '--seeds 100': 'PASS tools: caveCapture records the world seed  at .player.nearestEntranceDist'. With '--seeds 12': 'PASS ... at .config.gridSize'. With '--seeds 1' it correctly FAILs 'seed 1 not found'.
per_check.recommended_change: Use a differential search. Take a second snapshot in a world with a different seed, and require a leaf PATH whose value equals WORLD_SEED in both snapshots, i.e. it changes with the seed. At minimum, drop candidate paths whose value is the same in both worlds.

per_check.id: tools: caveCapture records where the player is in world space (world position or window origin)
per_check.why: The R state's window origin is (-960,-960). pox and poy search for the same number, so ONE leaf satisfies both (L295-296), and a snapshot that records only originX (y cannot be recovered) passes.
per_check.evidence: new probe p_originx_only (adds only `originX: windowOriginX`): 'PASS ... found .originX,.originX'. No other flips.
per_check.recommended_change: Require the x and y matches at DISTINCT paths, for both the origin pair and the world pair. Prefer a differential check: walk across a chunk line so the origin changes, then require that the found paths change by the origin or world delta.

per_check.id: tools: caveCapture records the player's own height (pos.floorZ), not just the mesh under them
per_check.why: The check only tells pos.floorZ apart from the mesh because today's floorH is the wrong layer (l0 = -7.62 on the cap). Once C1 is fixed, player.floorH equals the standing layer top, which equals h within 0.02. The check then passes although pos.floorZ is still not recorded, and KNOWN_BUGS would report this bug as fixed.
per_check.evidence: author's C1 FIX probe alone (p_c1fix): flips C1 AND 'PASS tools: caveCapture records the player's own height ...  at .player.floorH'. The snapshot has no floorZ field.
per_check.recommended_change: Take the R snapshot mid-jump: use the game's own jump input and tick until jumpAirborne is set and h is at least 0.5 h from every layer in the column. Also, or instead, use a differential: two snapshots at the same x,y with different pos.floorZ, requiring a path that tracks the change while player.floorH/ceilH do not. Exclude the player.floorH/ceilH paths from the search.

per_check.id: tools: caveCapture records the camera yaw
per_check.why: The yaw is a fixed 2.2 rad, searched by value in every leaf, including entrances[i].angle, which is rounded to 2 decimals (tolerance 0.01). On seeds whose entrance angle is 2.19-2.21, the unmodified game passes. The degree form (126 with tolerance 0.5) can also collide with integer counters.
per_check.evidence: unmodified game, '--seeds 275': 'PASS tools: caveCapture records the camera yaw  at .entrances.0.angle'. A scan of Cave Test seeds 1..4000 (h_angscan.js) found 17 seeds with an entrance angle rounding to 2.19-2.21 (72, 126, 219, 275, 331, ...).
per_check.recommended_change: Use a differential yaw. Snapshot the same state at yaw 2.2 and at yaw 0.9, and require one path whose value changes by 1.3 rad (or 74.5 degrees, modulo 2 pi).

per_check.id: tools: caveDiag().lastTransitionSnapshot is populated after walking from the surface into the cave

per_check.id: tools: the floor-rejection histogram's buckets never add up to more than its total

per_check.id: perf: game script evaluates without throwing
per_check.why: The check is LAB.load's own return value, so it cannot pass for the wrong reason. A BREAK probe (P7, a top-level throw) does make it fail, but because of a harness bug the FAIL line is parsed under a mangled id. The unittest and probe_testcase therefore see the real id as MISSING, not FAIL.
per_check.evidence: P7 via runprobes.py: raw stdout line 1 is 'FAIL perf: game script evaluates without throwing   [Error: probe: page script throws at load' and the next line starts 'Error: probe: page script throws at load'. The parsed ids are ['perf: game script evaluates without throwing   [Error: probe: page script throws at load'], and every original id is reported MISSING.
per_check.recommended_change: Keep the check. Fix the multi-line detail (see harness_bugs): the perf harness line 3 should pass only (LAB.loadError||'').split('\n')[0], or LAB.check should replace newlines in detail. Then add P7 as a BREAK probe expecting FAIL.

per_check.id: perf: Endless floor render buffer never overflows at any quality preset, pitch, dash FOV or heading
per_check.why: The number judged is not the buffer occupancy. It is derived as floorTotal - floorDistCull - floorFovCull - floorBehind (harness L58-60), which only holds while the game has exactly these three culls. A correct 'cull harder' change that counts into a NEW counter writes fewer cells, yet the formula reports more, so the check fails for the wrong reason. Sampling is adequate: for every preset, viewDist <= W*240-240 (500<=960, 900<=960, 1300<=1440, 1800<=1920), so the view circle stays inside the mesh from any position in the centre chunk. The result is also seed-independent (identical maxima on 7 seeds).
per_check.evidence: P9c adds an LOD cull beyond 1200 u counted in a new __caveStats.floorLodCull, which strictly reduces the cells written. runprobes.py P9c_lod1200_new_counter: 'FAIL (base PASS) perf: Endless floor render buffer ... <-- FLIP  ... ultra vd1800 W9 max=54413/40000'. Base is max=29788/40000.
per_check.recommended_change: Measure the real buffer. In floorPass(): set __caveStats.floorTotal = -1 and _drawFloorCellBuf.fill(NaN) before drawLayersFloor3D(). After it: ran = floorTotal >= 0, and written = the number of i with buf[3*i+1] === buf[3*i+1] (the pass is only full when written === capacity). Call it overflow only when written >= cap AND the formula > cap. Keep the formula for the detail text only. If the pass replaced _drawFloorCellBuf with a new object (a grow-fix), compare the formula with the new capacity.

per_check.id: perf: applying a quality preset rebuilds the window once when the chunk window changes and never otherwise
per_check.why: The id says 'once ... and never otherwise', but the observation window ends at applySettings plus one rAF flush (harness L109-112). Two consequences. (1) It misses a double rebuild that lands on the next frame. (2) It prescribes rAF timing: the suite's own BREAK probe (remove the rAF) is not a defect by the id's definition, because the next frame's updateChunks rebuilds exactly once and the window ends up the right size. commitPreset copies the Apply handler's assignments (L18010-18018) instead of calling handleSettingsClick. That is acceptable, because a real click at Apply's centre would hit N10's overlapping Day/Night toggle.
per_check.evidence: exp2.js --mode preset (commit, flushRaf, then 2 LAB.frame). Base: 'low W7->5 ... rebuilds_after_raf=1 ... rebuilds_after_2_frames=1'. With the suite's BREAK (p_norAF.py): 'low W7->5 rafs=0 rebuilds_after_raf=0 applied_after_raf=false rebuilds_after_2_frames=1 applied_after_2_frames=true' (same for high and ultra). With P4 (rAF centred one chunk off): 'low ... rebuilds_after_raf=1 ... rebuilds_after_2_frames=2', while the suite check stays 'PASS ... low W7->5 rebuilds=1 (want 1)' (runprobes.py P4_preset_double_rebuild: no flip).
per_check.recommended_change: Count rebuilds across commitPreset + LAB.flushRaf() + 2 LAB.frame() (with no keys held). Require total === expect, applied after that window, and the player's chunk unchanged across the frames (as a precondition). Replace the 'remove rAF' BREAK probe with P4 (expect FAIL), plus a never-applies BREAK (e.g. drop 'WINDOW_CHUNKS = settings.chunkWindow;').

per_check.id: perf: fixed Level 4 floor render buffer never overflows at any camera position, pitch, dash FOV or heading
per_check.why: floorPass() never resets __caveStats before calling drawLayersFloor3D. If the level pass returns early (a plausible 'fix' for the L12788 throw), the check reads STALE counters left by the Endless scenario and passes, with no Level-4 pass run at all. It is also mis-measured by the same formula issue as the Endless check: a correct new-counter cull is reported worse. Sampling is fine: a 1536-pass fine sweep found at most 46,627 against the harness's 46,596. The audit framing is incomplete: pitch 0 overflows too (43,290), not only pitch 1.4 + dash. The FAIL today is for the cited reason (FIX probe 01).
per_check.evidence: P1 ('if (!ENDLESS_MODE) return;' at the top of drawLayersFloor3D): 'PASS (base FAIL) perf: fixed Level 4 ... max buffered 27766 vs capacity 40000 ... at (720,480) pitch 0.00 heading 0deg'. 27766 is the stale Endless ultra pitch-max value (METRIC perf.floor.ultra.pitchmax.buffered_cells = 27766). exp4.js base: 'by pitch {"p0":{"f":43290,"w":40000},"p1.4":{"f":46596,"w":40000}}'. P9b (LOD cull at 2000 u, new counter): 'harness formula max 50226 ... cells actually written ... max 35950', and the suite check stays FAIL. l4sweep.js: 'fine sweep step 360 heads 16 passes 1536: max 46619 at (1620,540) 67.5deg'; 'local refine ...: max 46627'.
per_check.recommended_change: Same floorPass change as the Endless check: set the floorTotal = -1 sentinel before each pass, count 'did not run' as an EMPTY pass that fails the precondition, and base the overflow on real buffer occupancy. harness_bugs: Multi-line check detail breaks game_lab's parser. The perf harness L3 passes LAB.loadError, which _game_env L313 builds as String(e) + '\n' + e.stack. LAB.check (env L664-668) prints the detail raw, and game_lab _LINE (L55) needs the closing ']' on the same line. With P7 the parsed id is 'perf: game script evaluates without throwing   [Error: probe: page script throws at load' and the real id is MISSING. This probably affects every suite that reports loadError or another multi-line detail. Fix: in LAB.check, detail = String(detail).replace(/\s*\n\s*/g, ' | ').

floorPass() (harness L67-71) reads __caveStats without resetting it first, so a pass that returns early yields the previous pass's counters. This is the cause of the P1 vacuity: the Level 4 check read 27766, which is METRIC perf.floor.ultra.pitchmax.buffered_cells.

The local freshPage() (harness L37-45) restores 6 page-lifetime values; LAB.freshPage (env L585-591) restores 21 (gpLast, lastSelectDown, CONTROL_MODE, _physicsAccum, lastUpdate, menuOpen, dayTime, ...). Verdicts are unchanged when LAB.freshPage() is added (fullfresh.txt), but the far-site [STATE] counts move from 3+4 to 1+2, so known-bug margins depend on leftovers. Call LAB.freshPage() inside freshPage().

Frame-rate scenario: findSite runs only for the first rate (harness L462 'if (!seg) seg = findSite(...)'). The 60 fps turn is therefore measured at the relocated site and the 30 fps turn at spawn. Harmless for yaw, but the two runs are not identical set-ups.

seed_sweep.interpretation: No verdict changed against the default seed 424242, and two default runs gave byte-identical PASS/FAIL lines and details. The Endless buffer maxima are identical on every seed (the count is pure geometry). Numbers that did move: (1) far-site [STATE] line counts were s2 1+0, s31337 2+2, s99991 6+3, against 3+4 by default. Seed 2 kept the console known bug FAILing on a single random 0.5% event. That is harness fragility, not a game difference, and it is confirmed by the full-fresh (1+2) and reordered (4+3) variants on the same seed. (2) rgb cache finals of 56,131 / 38,743 / 14,156 are genuine location-dependent game behaviour (s2 is already at 30,873 after the NEAR site). (3) The walk ratio of 0.489 on s2 comes from a different near site (-380,72); this is the real game bug either way.

suspicions: The Endless buffer check samples only the spawn camera position. I verified by arithmetic that for every preset the view circle stays inside the mesh from anywhere in the centre chunk (viewDist <= W*240-240). This would stop holding if a hysteresis fix let the player sit far outside the centre chunk (more than 60 u at medium: 960-900).

The KNOWN_BUGS reason for Level 4 cites only 'pitch 1.4 + dash FOV', but exp4.js shows pitch 0 also overflows (formula 43,290 vs 40,000). A fix aimed only at the high-pitch under-foot skirt would leave the pitch-0 overflow, and the check would correctly keep FAILing. The KNOWN_BUGS text and audit D25 should say so.

The preset check's metric block runs one LAB.frame() between presets only for the first seed (si===0). In multi-seed runs this makes the page state differ between seeds (an extra frame, a possible uncounted rebuild). I did not observe a verdict effect.

proposed_checks.id: render: from inside the tunnel looking back out, the approach beyond the arch is drawn and no cap or surface underside is painted overhead
proposed_checks.design: Cave Test 12345 and 424242, every entrance. stand(E, -60, 0, 'bottom', E.angle + Math.PI) (the browser _OUTCEIL view). Precondition: |h - lowest walkable| < 0.05 under a ceiling with ceiling > h + EYE_H, and viewCells(cell with no ceiling and no cap and a walkable layer) >= 50 (open ground in the view cone). recordPass(drawLayersFloor3D). PASS iff (a) quads classified 'surface' with every vertex below the horizon >= 50 (the lit approach is visible through the mouth) and (b) overheadByClass.cap + overheadByClass.surface == 0. (a) is the reason to look out at all; (b) repeats the D5 contract for the reversed camera. Expected FAIL today on (b) (browser: 27.88% grass overhead from along -60).

proposed_checks.id: render: cave wall faces respond to the height of the cave ceiling beside them
proposed_checks.design: Cave Test 12345. Find a spot with render's capped-wall search (isCappedCaveFloor, headroom >= EYE_H, no grid wall), stand on the cave floor facing the wall, prepCamera, pitch 0. Record drawWalls3D three times: A as-is; B with every type-2 layer in floorMesh (l0..l4 where lNType==2) lowered by 0.5 h; C with every type-2 layer set to +5.0 h. B and C are data fixtures restored in a finally, like withOpenCaveCellsHidden. Precondition: A has >= 20 fills and the sorted vertex list of A differs from C (the pass does read ceilings above 0.1). PASS iff A differs from B: a ceiling at -1.2 h must shape wall tops as much as one at +5. Today caveCeilAt returns 0 whenever _ch <= 0.1 (L12129), so A == B -> FAIL. Not run by me; confirm C != A before trusting the check.

proposed_checks.id: render: an enemy's walk-cycle frame advances only while the enemy itself moves
proposed_checks.design: Endless 424242. Wrap the global ctx (L232, as persistence's withArcTo does) to record drawImage's first argument. Case 1 (idle, near): a surface enemy with vx=vy=0 and the camera 60 u away facing it (the render visibility setup: cam.x/y/ang, cam.z from the enemy's ground, depthBuffer=null). Call drawEnemies3D() at 8 clock values (LAB.advance(100) between); PASS needs all 8 frame canvases identical. Case 2 (walking, far): the same enemy with e.x advanced 1.5 u between draws and the camera at 1.1 x chaseRange; PASS needs >= 3 distinct canvases. Precondition: each draw issues >= 1 drawImage for the enemy (entityVisible3D non-null; raise viewDist for case 2 if needed). Today isMoving = camera dist in (10, chaseRange) (L14070), so both cases FAIL.

proposed_checks.id: enemies: an enemy that loses its target returns to its patrol route within 20 s
proposed_checks.design: Worlds: surface 424242, 777000 and cavetest 12345. For each enemy with >= 2 waypoints that EN_emb does not flag (cap 40 per world), use the chase-check setup: enemies=[e], player 100 u away with hasLineOfSight true, not market-safe. enemyTick until e.attackState != 'idle' (<= 600 frames). Precondition: the enemy chased and ended >= 40 u from its start. Then set shopMarker = pos (market-safe, L11420, so the chase condition is false while dist < 350) and enemyTick 1200 frames. PASS iff min distance to any of its waypoints <= 14 u (the game's arrival radius, L11295) in >= 95% of >= 30 trials. The 95% allows for residual F3 geometry. Restore shopMarker/enemies after each trial.

proposed_checks.id: enemies: the first physics tick after a Cave Test start neither re-centres the window nor clears cave enemies' underground flag
proposed_checks.design: LAB.startCaveTest(12345, {caveEnemies:true}); ug0 = count(enemies, e.underground). rec = LAB.countCalls('assembleWindow'); LAB.tick(1); rec.restore(). Precondition ug0 >= 5. PASS iff rec.calls == 0 AND ug1 == ug0. Measured today: calls 1, 25 -> 0. Report the two conditions separately in the detail, because the D19 fix alone satisfies only the second.

proposed_checks.design: LAB.startEndless(424242); set jumpAirborne=true, jumpVelZ=250 (the state step() leaves mid-jump, L10113). LAB.startEndless(424242) again (the Endless button path). Precondition: both were set before the restart. PASS iff jumpAirborne===false and jumpVelZ===0 right after start, and after LAB.tick(1) |h - topWalkable(spawn cell)| <= 0.05. Measured today: true/250 survive, h 0.00 -> 0.38 on tick 1.

proposed_checks.id: persistence: no other Settings hit area covers any part of the Apply button
proposed_checks.design: Reuse clickSettingsApply's layout step: settingsOpen=true, withArcTo(drawSettingsOverlay), areas=_settingsClickAreas. Precondition: >= 5 areas and one with action 'apply'. Sample the Apply rect on the existing 20x20 grid; PASS iff no sample falls in an EARLIER area (handleSettingsClick takes the first hit), i.e. hiddenFrac == 0. Today METRIC persistence.settings.apply_button_hidden_fraction = 0.55. The check just turns the existing metric into a verdict.

proposed_checks.id: persistence: finishing IMU calibration during Endless keeps the Endless world
proposed_checks.design: freshWorld(424242); record WORLD_SEED, worldW, grid.length, windowOriginX/Y. Set calibrating=true, hasYaw=false, lastRoll=baseRoll, lastPitch=basePitch, calStableMs=calNeedStableMs-60, then call onCalibUpdate() (what pollIMU does at L9896). Precondition: calibrating===false afterwards (calibration completed). PASS iff ENDLESS_MODE===true and WORLD_SEED, worldW, grid.length and the window origin are unchanged. Today L9854 calls resetLevel(1) and builds fixed level 1 -> FAIL.

proposed_checks.id: persistence: the cave-network memo and delta store stay bounded on a 40-chunk walk
proposed_checks.design: freshWorld(424242); teleportChunk east one chunk at a time for 40 crossings; after each, record Object.keys(endlessCaveNetworks).length, total entityDeltas bytes (census()) and Object.keys(chunks).length. Precondition: chunks loaded <= (WINDOW_CHUNKS+4)^2 at every step (eviction ran). PASS iff memo entries <= 49 at every step (7x7 regions covers a 9-chunk span plus the 3x3 generateChunk reach) and deltas <= 4 KB with no interaction. Today the memo is 30 after 4 crossings and deltas grow 11,200 B per crossing (METRICs).

proposed_checks.id: perf: the first frame on a freshly loaded page does not toggle the control mode
proposed_checks.design: LAB.freshPage() (restores page-load gpLast {buttons:0,valid:false} and lastSelectDown=false); LAB.startEndless(424242); cm0=CONTROL_MODE; n0=LAB.logCount; LAB.frame(). Control: repeat with LAB.releasePad() before the frame; CONTROL_MODE must stay put (proves the frame ran the pad path). PASS iff CONTROL_MODE===cm0 and no new '[CTRL]' log line. Measured: 2->1 with '[CTRL] toggled CONTROL_MODE= 1'; control 2->2. Must NOT use loot's releasePad or any other pad reset before the measured frame.

proposed_checks.id: perf: gamepad polling keeps at most one request in flight
proposed_checks.design: LAB.startEndless(424242). Replace hw.fetchJSON with a counter that returns a never-settling Promise. Set i2cEnabled=true, inputCompiled=true, running=true, gpPoll=null; startGamepadPolling(). Precondition: LAB.timers has a repeating 16 ms timer and its first call issues exactly 1 fetchJSON. Call it 9 more times with LAB.advance(16). PASS iff total calls == 1 (the ESP32 serves every request on one httpd task). Measured 10. Always stopGamepadPolling() and restore hw.fetchJSON.

proposed_checks.id: perf: an open overview map frame issues at most 5,000 fill calls
proposed_checks.design: Needs env support to keep the start timers: LAB.startEndless(seed, rng, {keepTimers:true}), or a scoped no-op of LAB.dropTimers as the scratch harness did. Start Endless 424242, LAB.runTimers() (the 100 ms auto-overview, L7648). Precondition: overviewActive===true. Count ctxCounters.fillRect + fill over one LAB.frame(); PASS iff <= 5,000 (a static map cached offscreen is one drawImage plus markers). Measured 78,418 fillRect/frame, and the game paused (0.0 u moved in 30 frames with W held). If the team decides auto-opening itself is the bug, use the alternative verdict 'player moves > 20 u in 30 frames after start'.

proposed_checks.id: perf: the floor pass parses no colour strings per quad
proposed_checks.design: Endless 424242, medium preset, LAB.prepCamera(), cam.ang=0, pitch 0. c=LAB.countCalls('parseInt'); drawLayersFloor3D(); c.restore(). Precondition: >= 1000 floor fills in the pass. PASS iff c.calls <= 0.01 x fills. Measured 5138 parseInt for 5138 fills (L12856/L12872); colours are known at assembly (l0Color..l4Color). Add the per-pass fill count as a METRIC next to it.

proposed_checks.id: perf: the walls pass samples no biome noise at render time
proposed_checks.design: Endless 424242: sweep 16 headings and keep the one with the most drawWalls3D fills. Count getBiomeAt, getWallBiomeRGB and smoothNoise calls (LAB.countCalls) during one drawWalls3D. Precondition: >= 500 fills. PASS iff all three counts are 0 (the window already holds wallColorR/G/B from assembly). Measured 1067 / 1067 / 2134 for 2048 fills. Report gradients created on the first and an identical second pass (318 / 318) as METRICs.

proposed_checks.id: perf: a window re-centre writes at most 2 console lines
proposed_checks.design: Endless 424242, open ground, 5 one-chunk re-centres via LAB.placeWorld. For each, take rec=LAB.countCalls('assembleWindow') and the LAB.logCount delta. Precondition: rec.calls == 5. PASS iff lines/rebuild <= 2. Today METRIC perf.chunkjitter.log_lines_per_rebuild = 19.7. A second check, 'a same-size re-centre reuses >= 90% of the window's typed-array bytes (same ArrayBuffer objects)', encodes the 17 MB/rebuild finding. It must land with the caves_transition shift-detection change (structural issue 5).

proposed_checks.id: perf: the Perf HUD fps readout matches the rate the loop is driven at
proposed_checks.design: Enable the Perf HUD the way its checkbox does. Drive 120 frames with LAB.frameAt(1000/30). Record #perfHudCanvas with a tools-style recording context and parse the fps figure from its fillText. Precondition: the HUD drew text on >= 60 frames. PASS iff fps is within 10% of 30. Today fps = 1000/avg JS time (L20774-20777) and the virtual performance.now makes JS time 0, so it reads 0 -> FAIL; an elapsed-ts formula reads 30.

proposed_checks.id: caves_geometry: no wall cell stands on a water cell
proposed_checks.design: Normal Endless seeds 424242, 777000, 1: generateChunk(cx,cy) for cx,cy in -8..8. Count i with ch.grid[i] && ch.floorMesh.water[i]. Preconditions: floorMesh.w == CHUNK_CELLS (shared indexing) and >= 1000 water cells in total. PASS iff wall-on-water <= 0.25% of water cells. The rationale is the generator's own rule 'Skip walls in water zones' (L4985). Measured 1/1075, 102/4762 (2.1%), 313/19157 (1.6%); with noiseSeed restored around terrainNoise: 0, 4 (0.08%), 0. The tolerance absorbs the remaining formula mismatch (terrainNoise+geography vs cHeights).

proposed_checks.id: caves_geometry: a cap raised above the natural surface never forms a cliff taller than STEP_UP with an open neighbouring cell
proposed_checks.design: In scanWindow, for every cell with a cap (type 4) and a ceiling where cap.z - surfaceH[i] > 1e-4, take each 4-neighbour with no ceiling, no cap and a walkable layer, and count cap.z - topWalkable(neighbour).z > 1.0 (STEP_UP, L7844). Precondition: >= 100 raised caps over all worlds (METRIC today 4555). PASS iff the count == 0. Measured 0/8/18/0 on ct12345/ct1/ct777/ct424242. The default worlds include ct1 and ct777, so this FAILs today.

proposed_checks.id: caves_transition: on open ground near a cave entrance, ambient light never brightens as the player gets closer to the entrance
proposed_checks.design: Isolates D9 from D2 with a data fixture. Endless 424242 spawn window, freezeDay(0.5): pick an open cell O with no ceiling/cap within 150 u and no real entrance within 300 u. Push {x:O.x, y:O.y, angle:0} onto deepCaveEntrances (restore in finally). For d in 130, 110, 90, 70, 50, 30, 10: place the player at O+(d,0) on the top layer and call updateDayNight(FIXED_DT) twice; record ambientLight. Precondition: playerUnderground false at every sample, and the ambient at d=130 equals the ambient without the fixture. PASS iff the sequence is non-increasing within 0.02 and amb(10) <= amb(130) - 0.1. Today L19380-19384 gives ~0.45 at 119 u rising to ~0.9 at 0 -> FAIL.

proposed_checks.id: caves_transition: walk-in: sun and fog change smoothly across the underground threshold
proposed_checks.design: On the existing axis walks, also read sunIntensity and fogFloor each tick (globals written by updateDayNight). Precondition: sunIntensity at the start >= 0.3 (noon via freezeDay). PASS iff |dSun| <= 0.2 x the surface sunIntensity and |dFogFloor| <= 0.05 on every tick. Today both jump in the tick playerUnderground turns true. A render companion checks the same flip for cave floor light: record the floor pass on the ticks just before and after the flip and compare the lit RGB of one cave-floor cell 60 u ahead; it must change by <= 25% luminance (floorLight 0.65 -> 0.3 today).

proposed_checks.id: physics: an airborne player never lands on a floor above its own height (no upward landing snap)
proposed_checks.design: Endless 424242 spawn window: find >= 20 open single-layer 4-neighbour cell pairs A->B with B.z - A.z in [0.4, 0.95], with no wall within 20 u and >= 300 u from any entrance. Place at A's centre 18 u from the shared edge facing B, boots {canJump:true}, jumpPressed=true, hold W with LAB.walkTo toward B+24 u (maxTicks 90). Per tick record prevAir, air and dh. Precondition: >= 20 jumps crossed into B while airborne. PASS iff no tick has prevAir && !air && dh > 0.35 (the transition suite's bound: STEP_UP eased 30%/tick = 0.30). Not measured by me.

proposed_checks.id: tools: window.caveTest runs to completion and returns a report
proposed_checks.design: Cave Test 12345: p = window.caveTest() (async, L1720). Drive with a loop of {LAB.runTimers(); LAB.flushRaf(); LAB.advance(16)} and a microtask turn between iterations (deno: await inside an async scenario; jsc: skip with a NOTE). Stop at 600 iterations. PASS iff the promise resolved to a non-null object, no exception was thrown or logged via console.error, and every point it teleported to (collect by wrapping placeWorld-equivalent pos writes, or from the returned report) is inside the window. Precondition: deepCaveEntrances.length >= 1.

proposed_checks.id: render: the cave arch never pops in and out while the player walks the approach
proposed_checks.design: Cave Test 12345, 424242 and 1, each entrance, perp offsets 0 / +40 / -40, layers top and bottom. Walk with LAB.walkTo from along +400 to +30 (real physics, so cam.z is what step() leaves). After each tick: prepCamera, recordPass(drawWalls3D) for the depth buffer, then recordPass(drawCaveEntrance3D). Count visible<->hidden transitions per walk. Precondition: the arch is visible on >= 1 tick of the walk. PASS iff transitions <= 1 per walk. My axis-only/top-layer placeWorld scan found 0 toggles, so this is a regression guard unless the off-axis runs reproduce E8.

structural_issues: KNOWN_BUGS only asserts that a listed check FAILs; it never asserts WHY. test_known_bugs_still_fail checks only by_id[k].ok (game_lab.py L276-280). A known-bug check that starts failing for a different reason (a PRECONDITION, a broken scenario, another mechanism) stays expected-green, and a fix that repairs one world while breaking another inside the same aggregated FAIL is invisible. No known bug fails on a precondition today (grep of every FAIL detail for 'PRECONDITION' found none), but nothing enforces that. Recommendation: each KNOWN_BUGS entry carries a detail regex (or at least 'no PRECONDITION in the detail'), and aggregated checks emit per-world sub-verdicts as METRICs so a partial regression shows.

FIX probes are validated only in their own suite. physics 'FIX D11' (picker returns the lowest walkable layer) flips caves_transition 'walk-in: the player never sinks more than a step height below every floor of its cell' PASS->FAIL: ct12345/E0 h -1.98 under floor -0.80 at along +227, end424242/E0 h -4.94 under -3.26, end424242/E1 h -3.10 under -1.74 (coupling run B). A later phase that applies probe texts as fixes would regress another suite. Recommendation: before a FIX probe is treated as a prescription, run it against every suite (the cross-suite probe matrix used here, about 1-2 min with HW1_GAME_JOBS=5).

caves_transition's FIX D3 probe (CAP_EXCL_SQ=0) turns the ambient monotonic check green only because D2's far-out roof keeps playerUnderground true before the 120 u blend zone. With CAP_EXCL_SQ=0 plus the D2 roof fix, the check fails with D9's signature on all 4 walks ('in 0.90->0.45 rises 0.45->0.89 at along 0; out ... drops 0.90->0.46 at along +120', coupling run C). The probe's PASS expectation and the KNOWN_BUGS text attribute to D3 what is partly D9.

physics C2 ('getFloorHeightAt never returns a stale floor height across a window shift') uses floorMesh.l0TopZ as its oracle (physics harness L275-277, L296), not a fresh read. With the D15 fix alone it PASSes. With the D15 fix plus a D6 fix inside getFloorHeightAt (return the lowest walkable layer) it FAILs: 'cave12345 inside assembleWindow 1221/69705 stale e.g. world(606,510) 2.07 vs -0.51 ... sweep: 1226 stale' (coupling run E), which is exactly the D6 cell count. Recommendation: compare each read with a second read after bumping _floorCacheTick.

caves_transition detects a re-centre by floorMesh object identity (harness L133 'if (floorMesh !== mesh)') and reads the pre-shift stack from the retained old mesh (L135 meshLayers(mesh, ...)). A G3 fix that reuses the window object would hide every shift, so the window-shift checks fail on 'no window shift' preconditions. A fix that reuses the typed arrays in place would make 'window shift: re-centring the window keeps the layer stack under the player unchanged' compare the new stack with itself and pass vacuously. Recommendation: detect shifts via windowOriginX/Y and copy the player's stack every tick.

LAB.frame() returns only the _loopErrCount delta (env L376-381). _pt-caught exceptions in handleInput, gameUpdate and every draw pass increment _ptErrors instead (L20576-20585, loop L21909-21920), so LAB.frame's 'errors this frame' misses them. Only render, perf-fixed-level and smoke read _ptErrors; physics C (LAB.frame across a shift), perf steady-state play and tools snapshots drive real frames without checking. The perf console check collects LAB.logs only (perf harness L184, L194), while game console.error lines (e.g. '[RENDER CRASH in platforms3D #1]') go to LAB.errors, so a render crash during steady play does not fail 'writes nothing to the console'. Recommendation: LAB.frame returns LAB.renderErrorsSince, and every frame-driven scenario asserts 0 new render errors and 0 new LAB.errors.

The env hides page-level defects on every start. _commonAfterStart calls LAB.dropTimers (cancels the 100 ms auto-overview, G5: measured 78,418 fillRect/frame and 0.0 u moved in 30 frames), sets CONTROL_MODE, and never runs a frame on page-load pad state (N11: measured 2->1 on a fresh page). smoke even asserts 'auto-overview timer was cancelled'. Element stubs discard addEventListener (env L271), so no suite can run the page's real handlers (btnEndless, terrainSelect, checkboxes, keys); LAB.startEndless/startCaveTest are replicas of those handlers, which the env's own header warns against. Recommendation: record listeners per element and add LAB.dispatch(id, type), add a keepTimers start option, and add a smoke check that LAB.startEndless and dispatching btnEndless 'click' produce the same state.

The helpers added after authoring are unused: grep over game_*_harness.js finds zero call sites for LAB.freshPage (only perf's private freshPage), LAB.releasePad (only loot's private one, which unlike LAB.releasePad does not reset lastSelectDown/lastStartMenuDown), renderErrorMark/Since, frameAt, setClock, countCalls, LAB.fx, LAB.cellWorld/cellCorner (caves_geometry keeps private copies at L49-56), standingLayer, logCount and record keepOnThrow. perf/physics wrap assembleWindow by hand and drive loop() with private driveFrames/speedAt. The copies have drifted: perf's freshPage resets 7 keys vs LAB.freshPage's 21. smoke does not exercise any of the new helpers, so they are untested.

Walks run at an idealised frame rate. LAB.tick calls handleInput and bumps _floorCacheTick once per 60 Hz physics step (env L386-395). The real loop calls handleInput once per rendered frame and bumps the cache once per draw, running 2-3 gameUpdates per frame below 60 fps. Every walk-based check (caves_transition, physics A/B/D, enemies, loot, persistence walks) therefore runs at 60 fps with a per-step cache flush: N1 and D15-class staleness inside multi-step frames are invisible to all of them. Recommendation: a --fps option that routes LAB.walkTo through LAB.frameAt.

Seeds and --seeds are inconsistent. Defaults differ per suite (Cave Test 12345 everywhere; 1 and 777 only in caves_geometry; normal Endless 424242 everywhere, 777000 in enemies/physics/render, 999983 in caves_geometry). N13 reproduces only with 'render --seeds 1' ('a camera on the cap above the cave draws no buried cave walls' FAILs: fillsFromCap(h=1.08,ug=0)=8), so the default run misses it. --seeds replaces BOTH Cave Test and Endless lists in enemies/physics/render/loot, but only the Cave Test list in caves_geometry and caves_transition (which use --normal-seeds/--endless-seeds); game_lab passes one --seeds to every suite. LAB.startCaveTest does not reseed Math.random while startEndless does (env L333-344 vs L358), and only some suites reseed by hand. An order-dependence test (caves_transition with --seeds 424242 / 12345,424242 / 777,424242) found all 45 non-ms ct/end424242 METRICs identical, so this is a latent risk, not an observed leak. Recommendation: one shared CT seed list {12345, 1, 777, 424242} for all cave suites and one --seeds semantics.

The persistence check 'the game keeps no state in browser storage (no localStorage/sessionStorage/IndexedDB/cookies)' encodes H1 (no storage) as desired behaviour, with a BREAK probe that fails on any localStorage use. It will report a fix of H1 as a regression. Reframe it as 'if storage is used, a save/reload round-trip restores X', or move it to a NOTE.

Runtime and isolation: the CLI runs suites serially, taking 1:54.75 wall / 157.9 s user for 174 checks (perf 22.0 s, enemies 21.1 s, caves_transition 12.8 s, render 11.8 s, physics 11.0 s, loot 9.8 s, caves_geometry 7.9 s, persistence 6.7 s, tools 5.4 s, browser 4.9 s, smoke 1.0 s). unittest uses the pool; probes are 105 extra full runs, opt-in. Within a suite all scenarios share one page, and only perf/persistence reset parts of it by hand (render runs its fixed level last 'on purpose' because a leaked save() would shift later baselines).

What a green run would NOT mean: no pixel is ever checked in unittest (browser half is manual; BROWSER_KNOWN_BUGS graded only with HW1_GAME_BROWSER_RESULTS); ESP32 transport/httpd/gzip, real gamepad/IMU, mouse/touch and 2D mode are untested; no frame-time budget exists (all *_ms are METRIC); walks run at 60 fps only; normal Endless covers only the nearest cave network per seed (--networks 1) and Cave Test forces plains terrain; fixed levels other than 1 and 4 are untested; sessions are < ~40 s of virtual play; consumers of D6 (enemy Z, wall bases, arch base) are unchecked; the in-cave views face inward only.

The enemies chase regression guard ('a lone enemy with line of sight reaches attack range within 10 s') steps only updateDayNight/updateEnemies/separateEnemies (enemies harness L59-66) and never step(), so the player's repelFromEnemies never runs. Its PASS says nothing about enemies reaching the player in play, which physics F1 shows they cannot (closest 16.3-22.4 u vs reach 12.4-17.2 u). Its LOS-2D FIX probe expectation ('... reaches attack range ...': PASS) is therefore also trivially met.
